name: Cholesterol synthesis
summary: Cytosol and ER, mainly liver, fed state. Acetyl-CoA → HMG-CoA (cytosolic HMG-CoA synthase; the mitochondrial isoform makes ketones) → mevalonate by HMG-CoA reductase — rate-limiting, NADPH, the target of statins. Mevalonate becomes isoprene units (IPP/DMAPP), which build farnesyl-PP, squalene, lanosterol and finally cholesterol. Insulin and thyroid hormone up-regulate HMG-CoA reductase; glucagon and cholesterol (via SREBP) down-regulate it. Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome = 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase deficiency.

acetylcoa.name: Acetyl-CoA
acetylcoa.notes: Cytosolic, exported from mitochondria as citrate (same route as fatty acid synthesis).

hmgcoa.name: HMG-CoA
hmgcoa.notes: Branch point: in mitochondria HMG-CoA lyase makes ketone bodies; in the cytosol it goes on to cholesterol.

ipp.name: Isopentenyl pyrophosphate
ipp.notes: The activated 5-carbon isoprene unit. Isoprenoids also make dolichol, CoQ and prenyl groups for proteins (Ras farnesylation).

fpp.name: Farnesyl pyrophosphate
fpp.notes: C15. Bisphosphonates (nitrogen-containing) inhibit FPP synthase in osteoclasts.

squalene.name: Squalene
squalene.notes: C30, linear: two FPP joined head to head.

dhc7.name: 7-Dehydrocholesterol
dhc7.notes: Reached after several more steps (demethylations, double-bond shifts). In skin, UVB converts it to vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol). Elevated in Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome.

cholesterol.name: Cholesterol
cholesterol.notes: Feeds membranes, bile acids (7α-hydroxylase), steroid hormones and vitamin D. Exported in VLDL; high cellular levels suppress SREBP-2.

hmgcs.name: HMG-CoA synthase
hmgcs.notes: Cytosolic isoform here; the mitochondrial isoform is rate-limiting for ketogenesis.

hmgcr.name: HMG-CoA reductase
hmgcr.notes: Rate-limiting; ER membrane; uses 2 NADPH. Statins competitively inhibit it → fewer hepatocyte sterols → SREBP up-regulates LDL receptors → lower LDL. Statin side effects: myopathy (↑ with fibrates, niacin, CYP3A4 inhibitors), hepatotoxicity. Induced by insulin and thyroid hormone; repressed by glucagon and cholesterol (SREBP, and sterol-triggered degradation).

mvk.name: Mevalonate kinase
mvk.notes: Deficiency causes hyper-IgD syndrome (periodic fevers) or mevalonic aciduria.

mvd.name: Mevalonate-5-pyrophosphate decarboxylase
mvd.notes: Uses a third ATP and releases CO₂ to give IPP.

fdps.name: Farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase
fdps.notes: Adds IPP twice: DMAPP → GPP → FPP. Inhibited by nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates (alendronate, zoledronate).

fdft1.name: Squalene synthase
fdft1.notes: Joins two FPP head to head; first step committed to sterols.

sqle.name: Squalene epoxidase
sqle.notes: Needs O₂ and NADPH. The fungal enzyme is inhibited by terbinafine.

lss.name: Lanosterol synthase
lss.notes: Cyclizes oxidosqualene into the four-ring sterol nucleus.

cyp51.name: Lanosterol 14α-demethylase
cyp51.notes: First of several steps from lanosterol to 7-dehydrocholesterol. The fungal homolog makes ergosterol and is the target of azole antifungals (fluconazole, ketoconazole).

dhcr7.name: 7-Dehydrocholesterol reductase
dhcr7.notes: Last step; uses NADPH. Deficiency = Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome (autosomal recessive): microcephaly, intellectual disability, 2–3 toe syndactyly, cleft palate, ambiguous genitalia in males, holoprosencephaly; ↑ 7-DHC, ↓ cholesterol.
